segments.text: Okay, today we're going to be talking
about ECS task definitions. So, you can
think of an ECS task definition as
something very similar to a launch
configuration or launch template for
EC2. It specifies all the details about
our ECS service that we're going to be
running. So, we have a task definition
which starts a task which runs in an ECS
cluster. That task may well or will
probably be started through an ECS
service. Um, but our task definition
allows us to set things like the CPU and
memory size. Uh, it allows us to attach
any volumes, any temporary volumes that
we need to add. It allows us to set the
task execution role. Uh, as well as the
task ro. The execution role is used to
do a pull of the items from the
registry. So you might need to give the
execution rule I am permissions to read
from ECR but then the task role itself
are the permissions the task that is
running will have and that doesn't
necessarily need to pull from ECR at all
and um we can have uh multiple
environment variables added to our
container as well also through the task
definition and we can also include
secrets within those environment
variables. So we can uh read things from
sequence manager or from an SSM
parameter store secure string and have
those securely passed as environment
variables. We also set port mappings and
uh we can have multiple containers
within a task and we do all that from
within the task definition. We can set
the order of which these multiple
containers will will start. So you might
have a sidecar container that does
logging for example sends logs to open
search. That container needs to be
started before the main container that
will be uh doing the actual work um is
running.
We have multiple versions of our task
definition in the same way as we have
multiple versions of a launch template.
And that allows us to uh do things like
have a production version and a
development version. But it also allows
us to just have newer versions of the
task happening and be able to roll back
easily if we have a problem. And that is
actually supported natively by the um
deployment mechanisms within ECS. Here
are some notes for you. Until next time,
enjoy the cloud.
